prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1238; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision in Baytown, Texas, where Driver 1 was turning left across traffic when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the driver's side. Driver 1 was operating the vehicle with Passenger seated beside them. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain at the scene and was evaluated by medical personnel. The described injuries are consistent with the direction and force of the impact. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses gave statements that match that account. Scene photographs show damage that is largely consistent with the reported impact pattern. Officers confirmed Passenger was present in the vehicle at the time of the crash, and both witnesses identified Passenger as an occupant. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Responding officers found no indication of prior damage to the vehicle, and none was reported by any party. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review of the statements and photographs.
